newsitem.title: USA: Orion Capital board adopts new rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Orion Capital board adopts new rights plan.

text.p: Orion Capital Corp said its Board of Directors adopted a new stockholder rights plan on Wednesday, to protect shareholders in case of a takeover and in light of a recent rise in Orion's share price.

Under the new plan, rights would be distributed as a dividend at the rate of one right for each share of common stock par value $0.01 per share, held by stockholders of record as of the close of business on September 16, Orion said in a statement.

The rights plan would "encourage potential acquirers of the company to negotiate with the Board of Directors so as to enhance the Board's ability to achieve the best possible value for all Orion Capital stockholders," Orion said.
The plan would deter coercive takeover tactics and impede a change of control of the company without shareholders receiving a full and fair price for their shares, it said.
It was adopted to replace a 1989 rights plan because Orion's share price has risen nearly 300 percent and now traded in a range near the original plan's exercise price, Orion said.
Each new right would initially allow shareholders to buy one unit of a share of preferred stock for $200, Orion said.

Rights would be exercisable only if a person or group acquired the beneficial ownership of 15 percent or more of the company's common stock or started a tender or exchange offer to own 15 percent, it said.
Orion would be entitled to redeem the rights at $0.01 per right at any time until 10 days following a public announcement that a 15 percent or greater position in the common stock had been bought.
Orion also said its board approved the redemption of outstanding rights issued under the original plan.
Holders of record on the common stock at the close of business on September 16 would receive $0.01 for each right being redeemed, Orion said.
Because of stock splits since the 1989 plan, the redemption price translated to $0.0064 per common share outstanding. Shareholders could expect to receive payment on or about October 1, Orion said.
The redemption would be treated as a dividend for tax purposes, the company said.
